title: On the Accuracy of the ALMA Flux Calibration in the Time Domain and across Spectral Windows
question: How accurate is the ALMA pipeline flux calibration between epochs and across spectral windows, tested with stable YSO calibrators in Band 7 ACA data?

what.value: ALMA calibrator catalog fluxes and spectral indices (queried April 2020)

evidence.quote: We thus queried the flux of each grid calibrator in April 2020 and compared its flux and spectral index with the values used by the pipeline

external_data.citation: ALMA calibrator catalog (not cited as a paper)

recipe.goal: Extract continuum per calibrator and epoch
recipe.method: Dirty cubes, sigma-clipped spectra in 3 arcsec aperture, uv-plane point-source fit with flat spectral index
assumptions: YSO calibrators stable in flux and spectral index

recipe.method: MCF = mean flux over 7 epochs divided by epoch flux; rFCF = average of 4 MCFs
assumptions: YSO calibrators stable to ~3-5% from JCMT monitoring

recipe.method: Compare original pipeline vs April 2020 catalog fluxes, rescale visibilities, recompute MCFs and rFCFs
Per-spw normalized MCFs; Gaussian fits to scatter histograms; power-law fit vs frequency; Monte Carlo of 16 normalized MCFs repeated 10000 times
assumptions: Width of distribution is sum of two uncorrelated random errors; systematic frequency-dependent terms negligible
